transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CTO, Sapphire), Ben Wallace (Lead ML Eng), Samir Kapoor (Infra), Elena Gomez (Product)
Links shared: deck: https://rwd.example.com/decks/sapphire-readiness.pdf; benchmark sheet: https://rwd.example.com/bench/saph-tokenplan.xlsx

Summary: quick discovery focused on p95 targets for streaming chat and burst capacity. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem) based on latency SLOs, cost, and security controls. They asked for benchmark plan and SOC2 artifacts; agreed to POC checklist call next week.

Topics: p95 latency objectives, concurrent sessions and expected bursts, streaming token/sec test cases, KV/prefix cache behavior, encryption/KMS and SSO, dedicated capacity sizing, fallback strategies.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alicia Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm alicia from redwood inference. quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya Nair: hi this is priya, CTO at sapphire. we'll go over why we're here, our p95 goals and traffic profile.
[00:15] Ben Wallace: ben here, lead ml eng. i'll talk workload shapes.
[00:19] Marcus Rivera: marcus, se, i'll cover latency and benchmarking approach.
[00:25] Samir Kapoor: samir infra, i'll cover network and VPC constraints.
[00:30] Alicia Chen: awesome. quick agenda — scope SLOs, current infra, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, benchmarking plan, next steps.
[00:40] Priya Nair: to set context, we run a conversational assistant embedded in our product. typical session is 150-300 tokens, but we get spikes during product launches, 900 concurrent sessions in region during peak, sustained 200 qps on average. p95 latency target for streaming responses is 300 ms end-to-end from our api-gateway to first token ideally.
[01:05] Ben Wallace: and we do partial streaming — we need first token within 250-350 ms p95, and tail tokens should be steady but not exceed 600 ms for long completions. also we have multi-turn context with kv cache usage.
[01:25] Marcus Rivera: okay, that helps. couple clarifying q's — is that 300 ms from your edge or from redwood-hosted environ?
[01:33] Priya Nair: from our edge, so includes our network hops to the model endpoint, but we want redwood to be responsible for the bulk of the inference latency.
[01:42] Alicia Chen: got it. when you say kv cache — are you talking about prefix caching for known intents, or a more persistent kv-store you manage?
[01:51] Ben Wallace: prefix caching — we pin the first 5-6 tokens and want the system to reuse kv-cache to avoid re-computation. we call it K V cash sometimes in our notes ha — sorry for the spelling.
[02:04] Marcus Rivera: totally, we have prefix/KV cache support in the runtime, though sometimes the transcription may show it as K V cash in our logs too. it reduces token work a lot for multi-turn.
[02:14] Samir Kapoor: on network — we have strict egress rules. if we go hosted we need a peering setup and strict CIDR whitelisting. private deployment is attractive for compliance but ops team shy about managing on-prem GPU fleets.
[02:28] Priya Nair: security is a big factor — saml sso, kms integration, audit logs — we need SOC2 type II and ability to integrate with our key manager for secrets.
[02:40] Alicia Chen: we can provide SOC2 reports and KMS integrations, plus SSO via SAML or OIDC. for private on-prem we support customer-managed HSM as well. we'll attach the whitepaper.
[02:50] Ben Wallace: great. on the hosting question — what's the delta in p95 we usually see between hosted and dedicated? numbers please.
[02:58] Marcus Rivera: rough ballpark — for streamed first-token p95 on a 4xA100 dedicated pool with batching optimized for short sequences, customers see ~120-200 ms for 256-token context. hosted may be comparable but depends on region and multi-tenant load — we'd guarantee throughput more with Dedicated. caveat: these are infra-level numbers; end-to-end will include your network.
[03:20] Priya Nair: we need clearer numbers at the token/sec level. during a promo, we expect token ingress bursts up to 5k tokens/sec sustained for 30s, and then falls back. our steady-state is ~1.2k tokens/sec. how does redwood handle burst vs steady?
[03:37] Marcus Rivera: we have autoscaling and burst pool options — Dedicated gives you reserved capacity, plus configurable burst to avoid cold starts. Hosted can autofanout but is subject to queueing during extreme bursts unless you purchase burst credits. We usually propose a stress test: synthetic traffic scripts that model your 5k tokens/sec burst and 900 concurrent sessions for 30s, then verify p95 and tail latency.
[04:00] Ben Wallace: yes, please. also quantization — we run 8-bit models in prod to reduce latency/cost. does redwood's runtime support server-side quantized kernels and maintain p95?
[04:12] Marcus Rivera: yes, we support INT8/4 quantization paths and the kernel selector chooses optimized code paths. there can be small throughput differences; we'll include quantized vs fp16 runs in the benchmark plan.
[04:25] Priya Nair: what about streaming vs non-streaming token/sec? we need both — first-token p95 and tokens/sec sustained for a 600-token completion.
[04:34] Marcus Rivera: recommended testcases: (A) streaming short (150-300 tokens) 900 concurrent sessions, (B) burst token flood 5k tokens/sec for 30s, (C) long completion 600 tokens at steady 1.2k tps. We'll report p50/p95/p99 and token/sec throughput and GPU utilization.
[04:52] Alicia Chen: will you want Redwood to run these in our hosted infra first, or do you prefer to pilot on a Dedicated node or bring-your-own private box?
[05:01] Priya Nair: we'd like to start hosted for speed but we want to compare dedicated and private as options. hosted for initial benchmarking then check Dedicated for committed latency and private for compliance runbook.
[05:12] Samir Kapoor: for private, our infra team is concerned about cluster ops; do you provide an on-prem packaging and install playbook?
[05:20] Marcus Rivera: yes, we have a Private deployment package and an ops-runbook. for air-gapped installs there's a checklist. we'll share that doc.
[05:27] Elena Gomez: on success criteria — product care about p95 < 350 ms for first token and < 600 ms tail at p95 during peak. infra wants no more than 2% request failures during 30s bursts.
[05:40] Ben Wallace: also want stability across model versions — we need a canary rollout and automatic fallback to a slightly smaller model if p95 spikes.
[05:48] Marcus Rivera: Redwood supports rollouts and automatic fallback to compatible model variants; we can run A/B canaries and metric-based rollback. we'll propose thresholds.
[05:57] Priya Nair: great. on telemetry — we need token-level visibility and per-route latency breakdowns. is that in console?
[06:05] Alicia Chen: yes, the Redwood Console provides token-level cost/latency breakdowns, and tracing hooks; we can add your routes to dashboards.
[06:13] Ben Wallace: a lot of our sessions use few-shot prompts which increase prefix size. how does prefix caching help with cost and latency?
[06:21] Marcus Rivera: prefix caching means you avoid recomputing KV for the prefix each call; we cache and reuse the KV caches. this can reduce per-request work by 30-60% depending on prefix length. we'll measure with your actual prompt sets.
[06:34] Samir Kapoor: network egress — if hosted, are there options for private peering? we need to avoid public egress.
[06:41] Alicia Chen: yes, peering and private-link options are standard for enterprise hosted customers. for Dedicated we can also place pools in your VPC.
[06:49] Priya Nair: ok, any known trade-offs with autoscaling and streaming — does scaling cause noticeable p95 spikes?
[06:56] Marcus Rivera: cold starts for new replicas can add latency. continuous batching and warm pools reduce this. Dedicated with reserved capacity avoids most scaling spikes; hosted can be tuned with warm pools and burst credit. we'll capture these behaviors in the POC tests.
[07:12] Ben Wallace: curious about token/sec measurements — do you report tokens/sec per model or aggregated per pool?
[07:18] Marcus Rivera: both — we can show tokens/sec per-model, per-pool, and per-route. the benchmark sheet will include GPU utilization and tokens/sec timelines so you can correlate latency spikes with saturation.
[07:30] Priya Nair: ok, what do you need from us to run the initial benchmarking?
[07:34] Alicia Chen: samples of prompt templates, distribution of session lengths, expected concurrency windows, and any auth/network constraints.
[07:41] Priya Nair: we'll send prompt templates and a histogram for token lengths (p50/p95/p99) and a sample of traffic traces.
[07:48] Ben Wallace: also include any model variants you want tested — quantized and fp16. we'll run both.
[07:53] Marcus Rivera: perfect. i'll propose the benchmark testcases and schedule. plan is: hosted smoke run, dedicated comparatives, and optionally private deploy checklist.
[08:03] Priya Nair: timeline-wise, we aim to decide deploy mode by end of november. can we have the hosted smoke and numbers by two weeks?
[08:11] Alicia Chen: yes, two weeks is doable for hosted smoke. dedicated comparatives might take another week for reserved pool allocation.
[08:18] Samir Kapoor: final Q — encryption keys must live in our KMS for private; for hosted is BYOK via KMS federation supported?
[08:26] Marcus Rivera: yes, for hosted we support BYOK with KMS federation and for private you can bring an HSM. we'll document the flow.
[08:34] Speaker 1: (murmur) also we might test model fallbacks to smaller quantized models if latency spikes.
[08:40] Alicia Chen: noted. i'll attach a sample rollback policy.
[08:44] Priya Nair: thanks, this was helpful. next steps?
[08:48] Alicia Chen: recap — alicia will send SOC2 and compliance docs; marcus will share benchmark plan + test scripts; priya will share traffic histograms and prompt sets. we'll schedule POC checklist the week of Nov 10.
[08:59] Ben Wallace: and we'll review cost numbers for dedicated 4x A100 and hosted estimate.
[09:05] Marcus Rivera: i'll include quantized vs fp16 cost and perf delta in the estimate.
[09:10] Priya Nair: great, thanks everyone.
[09:13] Alicia Chen: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
